newsitem.title: USA: Sen. Lott sees U.S. budget deal relatively quickly.
newsitem.headline: Sen. Lott sees U.S. budget deal relatively quickly.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he believed lawmakers could work out final budget and tax legislation acceptable to the White House in relatively short order.
The House and Senate have passed differing verions of legislation cutting Medicare, Medicaid and other programs over five years and providing a net $85 billion tax cut.

"I think we have a good opportunity to get an agreement between the House and Senate and the administration that we can accept and that can be signed (by the president)," he told reporters. "We think we can find agreement relatively quickly."

Lott called on Clinton to show some leadership on the issue of Medicare. The Senate version of the budget bill would force affluent seniors to pay higher Medicare premiums and raise the program's eligibility age to 67 from the current 65.
"I hope the president will step up directly to the strong action taken in the Senate over Medicare," Lott said.
He said Congress would have to make some compromises on taxes, saying Republicans wanted "the strongest possible tax relief bill for the American people" that Clinton is willing to sign.
Earlier Tuesday, U.S. House Majority Leader Richard Armey said he expected Congress would pass a tax bill that President Clinton would sign.
